name: The Boar Hunter
summary: Talin Keeneye asks for help in Coldridge Valley, where crag boars threaten the trails. The dwarf hunter wants young recruits to thin their numbers so seasoned hunters can track in peace.

sections.title: A Crowded Valley
sections.body: Coldridge Valley gives young mountaineers and scholars of Ironforge a quiet, protected place to train. In the harsh winter, its wildlife can grow restless and numerous. Talin Keeneye, a veteran hunter stationed outside Anvilmar, has seen small crag boars multiply across the valley. Their attacks threaten anyone walking the snowy trails.

sections.title: Tending the Snows
sections.body: Hunting gives dwarves meat, hide, and practice in the field. When game grows numerous and attacks on sight, its numbers must be cut. By thinning the crag boars across the valley slopes, young adventurers show they can handle a fight. Their work also gives local hunters room to pursue game without being overwhelmed.

aliases: who gives the boar hunter quest
faq.answer: Talin Keeneye is a dwarven hunter stationed in Coldridge Valley, near Anvilmar. He tracks game in the snow and teaches novice adventurers how to deal with hostile beasts.

faq.q: Why are the crag boars such a problem?
faq.answer: Small crag boars have grown unusually numerous in Coldridge Valley, and they attack without provocation. Their numbers make travel and hunting dangerous for locals.

faq.q: Where can the crag boars be found?
faq.answer: Small crag boars roam the open snowy plains and lightly forested areas around Anvilmar, throughout Coldridge Valley.

faq.q: Does this quest connect to a larger threat in the valley?
aliases: is there a follow up quest
faq.answer: No. Troggs trouble the dwarven outposts, but the crag boars are a local wildlife problem. Thinning their numbers keeps the footpaths safer and lets Talin hunt in peace.

faq.q: What makes crag boars suited to Dun Morogh?
faq.answer: Crag boars are tough, thick-hided swine that endure Dun Morogh's freezing temperatures. Their aggressive nature and sharp tusks help them forage through frozen soil and defend themselves from mountain predators.

faq.q: Why doesn't Talin Keeneye kill the boars himself?
faq.answer: Talin says the aggressive boars have made his hunts unpleasantly dangerous. He asks eager newcomers passing through Anvilmar to thin their numbers so he can return to his usual tracking.

angles.text: Mountain life means sharing the land with fierce wildlife. As a young dwarf, thinning the aggressive crag boars around Anvilmar is a rite of passage beyond the forge.
As a hunter, you can follow Talin Keeneye's plain approach to tracking: aim true, respect the beasts, and clear the brush when game turns hostile.
As a gnome refugee newly arrived from Gnomeregan, facing Dun Morogh's fierce wild boars is a hard introduction to life in rugged dwarf country.
